section_plan.title: Objective
content_bullets: Develop novel deep learning methods enabling neural networks to generalize across diverse physical environments and boundary conditions in physics domains
Address gaps in applying DL to physics problems where standard computer vision techniques fail
Demonstrate utility on three Navy-relevant physics tasks: underwater acoustics, RF propagation, and structural health monitoring
notebook_topics: differences between CV/NLP and physics applications

section_plan.title: Motivation and Background
content_bullets: Neural networks excel in CV/NLP but struggle with physics domain generalization
Emerging field of Simulation Intelligence merges scientific computing with neural networks
Current NN solutions lack evidence of good test performance over entire range of physically realizable inputs
Gap: no prior studies on generalization in physics domains
citation_hints: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Chen et al.)
Physics Meets Machine Learning survey (Meng et al.)

section_plan.title: Research Hypotheses
content_bullets: H1: CV/NLP generalization methods will improve physics task generalization
H2: Physics equations, symmetry, and invariances can improve domain-specific generalization
Two technical challenges: identifying cross-domain techniques (TC1) and deriving domain-specific methods (TC2)
citation_hints: Generalization studies in deep learning (Chatterjee, Dziugaite, Jiang et al.)
Data augmentation in NMT (Li et al.)

section_plan.title: Application Domains
content_bullets: Underwater acoustics: transmission loss prediction from ocean properties using PALIS baseline
RF propagation: atmospheric EM propagation using COAMPS data, modified from acoustics approach
Structural health monitoring: real-time damage detection on naval platforms using MINC baseline

section_plan.title: Neural Operator Frameworks
content_bullets: Neural operators learn mappings between infinite-dimensional function spaces
Neumann Series Neural Operator (NSNO) selected for Helmholtz equation applications
NSNO achieves 60% error reduction vs standard FNO on 2D Helmholtz problems
Enables universal physics solvers requiring single training cycle across diverse parameter spaces

section_plan.title: Methodology
content_bullets: Task 1: Establish baselines for three domains using existing PALIS, COAMPS, and MINC implementations
Task 2: Investigate CV/NLP generalization properties (data augmentation, architecture, hyperparameters) in physics contexts
Task 3: Develop physics-informed generalization techniques using domain equations, symmetries, and invariances
Evaluate using complexity, norm, and sharpness measures adapted for physics ML

section_plan.title: Underwater Acoustics Results
content_bullets: PALIS network trained on SSP-to-TL mapping using UVCGAN_V2 architecture
Ray-trace vectors as secondary input channels improve quality with reduced runtime
Frequency-specific training experiments (fRange1, fRange2, fRange3) to assess generalization
Mixup data augmentation effects on train/test metrics

section_plan.title: RF Propagation Results
content_bullets: Modified refractivity prediction in marine atmospheric surface layer
Neural network trained on COAMPS NWP data for propagation factor estimation
Multi-frequency approach (S-band and X-band) for diverse atmospheric conditions
Comparison of scaled vs unscaled input representations

section_plan.title: Structural Health Monitoring Results
content_bullets: Physics-first approach using Gabor representation of time-series wavepackets
100% detection accuracy achieved on laboratory data
Automated robotic gantry for generating large experimental datasets with simulated damage
Neural network architecture leveraging time-frequency domain physics
